target_customer: Website owners wanting easy sign-in and everyday users who did not want to manage many passwords
problem: OpenID sign-in required users to remember an identity URL. Clickpass let users sign in with one click using a single identity.
business_model: free sign-in widget for sites, no revenue model found

founders.name: Peter Nixey
founders.background_notes: Only founder listed on the YC page. Education and employers not given.

founders.name: Immad Akhund
founders.background_notes: Named with Peter Nixey as a founder of Clickpass in TechCrunch coverage (https://techcrunch.com/?p=14891) and by Dealroom; the YC page lists only Nixey.

technical_complexity.rationale: A widget that built login URLs from a username and mediated OpenID flows was ordinary web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: OpenID was an open standard, and JanRain RPX, Facebook Connect and Google Friend Connect arrived in late 2008.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook Connect and Google Friend Connect left beta in December 2008, JanRain launched RPX in October 2008, and Clickpass was bought by SynthaSite in December 2008 and later by Janrain in 2012 per aggregators.

market_need_then: OpenID adoption was growing but sign-in was awkward for ordinary users; Clickpass launched March 2008 and was praised for its simple interface.

identity.visual_style: simple interface with an orange button per Simon Willison's 2008 post

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch and developer blogs at launch; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Some press at launch but no evidence of lasting recognition.

outcome_analysis: Clickpass launched its OpenID one-click sign-in in March 2008 after the YC Summer 2007 batch, but the identity space quickly filled with JanRain RPX, Facebook Connect and Google Friend Connect in late 2008. The company was bought by SynthaSite (Yola) in December 2008 per Mergr and later folded into Janrain, with undisclosed terms and no substantial funding found.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503. Acquisitions come from aggregators (Mergr, CB Insights); the Janrain 2012 acquisition date is 2012-11-01 or 2012-11-12 depending on source. Funding: CB Insights 20K versus Dealroom 337K, and one blog says 330,000 dollars; none are verified rounds. One source names Immad Akhund as cofounder but the YC page lists only Peter Nixey, so he is not listed. YC page location conflicts (London versus San Francisco). The timeline of the acquirers is aggregator based. The JanRain RPX launch (2008-10) is later than founding so it is not listed as a competitor. Completeness pass: Round added: a press article (TechCrunch, also an inkl elevator pitch item) says the founders had raised 330,000 dollars; no date or investors given. Dealroom says about 337K from Y Combinator and Lowercase Capital and CB Insights says 20K over four rounds, conflicting, not summed.
